capabilities: Import an Apple Health export (Export.zip or Export.xml) as a stream into a local cache
Browse metrics in a dashboard with sparklines, time series, and period presets
Compare two metrics on one chart with separate axes
Write value tables as .md or .csv files into a chosen vault folder
Copy today's health values into daily-note properties for Bases and Dataview
extras: Desktop-only (isDesktopOnly: true). The manifest carries the note 'This plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.' Full documentation (getting started, troubleshooting) is linked on an external docs site. No network calls; the cache file health-cache.json is gitignored.
motivation: Apple's Export.xml reaches several gigabytes (2.6 GB with 5.7 million records in the author's test), and ordinary XML parsers load it all into memory and crash; the author built a streaming parser that keeps only compact daily aggregates.
problem: Obsidian runs in Electron with no HealthKit access, and Apple's multi-gigabyte Export.xml crashes ordinary in-memory XML parsers, so health data has no path into the vault.

relations.evidence: reads Apple Health exports and makes the data searchable and visualizable inside your vault
so Bases and Dataview can combine them with the rest of your vault
